prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realisation of the optical lattice clock based on magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms, bringing atomic frequency standards to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I keep optical lattice clocks (B002) as my single-part proposal, and the first-round exchange has strengthened rather than weakened it. Five of eight members now name it as their preferred part, all with the same two names and the same core credit, and it is the only candidate that members of different subfields place first or near first for the same reasons. In answer to the chair's first question, the citation recognises something the 2005 and 2012 prizes did not: the 2005 prize gave us the frequency comb to count optical cycles, and the 2012 prize gave control of single trapped quantum systems, whereas the magic-wavelength lattice lets an ensemble of many neutral atoms be interrogated with the light shift of the clock transition cancelled, which is what turned optical clocks from a single-ion accuracy exercise into a stability and accuracy regime near 10^-18 with millimetre-scale gravitational redshift sensitivity. That is a new measurement capability, independently reproduced at RIKEN/Tokyo, JILA, SYRTE, PTB and NIST, and the interpretation is stable. The credit is compact: Katori for the concept and first demonstration, Ye for taking the strontium lattice clock to the accuracy and stability frontier. I propose one part only, because no second part that I can attribute within the three-name limit is both mature and clean.
statement.case_against: The reservation I cannot remove is the cumulative-recognition one: a sceptic can read lattice clocks as a spectacular refinement of a line already honoured in 2005 and 2012, and a citation must therefore be written around the neutral-atom magic-wavelength lattice and not around precision metrology in general. The credit boundary is also real. Takamoto, Lemonde, Ludlow and Derevianko on the theory of the lattice shifts all made contributions that a two-name prize passes over, and I accept that a Katori-Ye allocation is defensible rather than unassailable. Finally, the second has not been redefined. I do not regard that as a reason to wait, since a prize that rests on established performance and independent reproduction does not depend on a metrological convention, but I recognise it as a legitimate point of view.

responses.point: Danielsson keeps the experimental Higgs discovery (B053) first on maturity and scale of consequence, while acknowledging that three founding-era names cannot fairly stand for two collaborations of thousands and naming B002 and B038 as better-attributed fallbacks.
responses.response: I agree with you on the science: the discovery is secure, confirmed by two experiments and a decade of coupling measurements, and the 2013 prize left it unrecognised. Where we differ is on whether an honest three-name rule exists. You identify the weakness yourself, and I have not seen a principled criterion in round 1 that separates founding leadership from the discovery-year spokespersons and analysis conveners who delivered the 2012 result. Until one is offered, I cannot put a prize that I expect to be challenged on credit above one whose credit is compact. I have kept B053 as an alternative on the strength of your argument. Your own statement that B002 is a better-attributed alternative is, to me, the nub of the matter.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B038), arguing that the 2011 quantitative prediction followed by the 2018 discovery that matched the predicted angle is the cleanest theory-plus-experiment attribution among the strongest candidates, and says he could accept B002 as the second part of a two-part prize.
responses.response: I accept that B038 is the cleanest theory-plus-experiment story on the list, and that the flat-band prediction matched by experiment is the kind of result I value. I disagree on timing. With the superconducting mechanism still open and the experimental credit to Jarillo-Herrero standing in for Cao and the early authors, I would be awarding a platform before its central lesson is known. I considered your two-part suggestion, B002 with B038. It would solve nothing about B038's maturity and would add a second set of credit objections to the first. I therefore remain with a single part, but I rank B038 as my first alternative, and I would revisit it as the leading candidate in a later year if the mechanism question settles.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B038 on conceptual economy, a minimal effective model organising a large phenomenology, and notes that experimental credit is shared with Cao and collaborators and that B002 is the safer choice if maturity is valued above breadth.
responses.response: Your last sentence states my position fairly: I do put maturity first, and I take your point that the conceptual content of the flat-band model is greater than the quantitative advance of the clocks. I would add that the clocks are also more than a quantitative advance, since cancelling the light shift with a magic wavelength is a conceptual idea in the same sense as an effective model that organises phenomenology. Your request that the B038 citation not claim an explanation of superconductivity is right, and if the committee ever turns to B038 I would support wording that says prediction and discovery of correlated states only. I do not think that exceeding the experimental credit to Jarillo-Herrero can be settled by wording alone.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B002 first, discloses a documented research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder with a possible perceived link through Ye and JILA, and asks whether he should abstain on B002.
responses.response: I share your first choice and your reading that the credit is compact and the physics stable rather than provisional. On your question, a research stay in a laboratory associated with an earlier prize and not with Ye's lattice-clock programme is a perceived connection that should be recorded, and I would record it, but I do not think it requires abstention, since B002 would still have four other explicit supporters and your reasoning is independent of the connection. I would ask that the final ballot note it. On B033, I remain cautious for the reasons I gave in round 1: the credit is split among several ion-trap laboratories and the 2012 prize already honours the control on which it builds.

responses.point: Lindroth warns that the clock community is divided on how credit should be split between the lattice proposal and the long JILA programme, and says that the IceCube citation would say more about a window opened than about what was found.
responses.response: Your reading of the division in credit is the most useful caution in the round, and I take it as a reason to write the citation narrowly, on the lattice clock itself, and to credit Katori for the concept and Ye for the accuracy frontier, and not to claim either as the sole origin. I accept your criticism of IceCube: the diffuse flux is secure but the source populations are not understood, and my own proximity to astroparticle work argues against my pressing it. I have therefore dropped B043 from my alternatives.

uncertainties: Whether the committee reads the neutral-atom magic-wavelength lattice as a sufficiently new advance beyond the frequency comb (2005) and single-quantum-system control (2012).
Whether a Katori-Ye allocation will withstand the claims of Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Derevianko.
Whether the redefinition of the second should be awaited, which I do not think necessary but which several members do.
Whether B038 will mature enough, with the pairing mechanism and the experimental credit settled, to overtake B002 on a later ballot.
Whether any principled three-name rule can be found for B053.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with B002, B038 or B053 or the credited names. My documented connections are PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur, and my field is astroparticle physics, so IceCube (B043) is scientifically close to my own work. I have removed it from my alternatives and record that proximity. I record Kroll's disclosed perceived connection to B002 and the recusal intentions of Johansson on B017 and Olsson on B055.
